name: DesktopSideBar fixes
description:
**Conversation Summary**

1. User requested that the Windows menu receive focus on open and close on blur.
2. I explored `WindowsMenu.vue`, `WindowsMenuItems.vue`, and related reka-ui Menubar patterns.
3. I proposed modifying `src/components/main-menu/WindowsMenu.vue` with a trigger ref, content ref, `tabindex="-1"`, and `@focusout`/`@pointerdown` handlers.
4. Added `pointerDownInside` state plus `elOf`, `focusMenu`, `onContentPointerDown`, and `onFocusOut` methods to manage focus and blur behavior.
5. Result: menu focuses on open and closes on blur, while still preserving keyboard-open focus and in-panel clicks.

This library injects content with the data-reka-poppe... [5] javascript - Z-Index on Popper menu? - Stack Overflow URL: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/52827235/z-index-on-popper-menu Using the React Portal API, the Material-UI Popper component renders by default outside the DOM hierarchy of the parent tree, this explains why it res... ``` ``` Read 1 file(s) | Successfully read: src/components/main-menu/WindowsMenuItems.vue ``` ``` Read 1 file(s) | Successfully read: src/components/UserInfoPanel.vue ``` Let me confirm how reka-ui renders the popper wrapper z-index by fetching its source.I now have a clear understanding. Let me verify the Tailwind z-index scale and the sidebar store flag before finalizing. ``` Read 1 file(s) | Successfully read: tailwind.config.js ``` ``` Search completed: 3 queries executed, 30 documents found ``` I've completed my analysis. Here's my understanding and proposed plan. ## 1. Analysis & Pre-Thinking ### Core Requirements Two related bugs in the **desktop hover sidebar** (`src/components/layout/DesktopSidebar.vue`): 1. **Project detail modal never appears.** Clicking the project selector opens a modal, but the sidebar collapses on `mouseleave` (because the modal overlay now sits under the pointer), which unmounts `ProjectDetailt` and destroys the modal state. 2. **WindowsMenu renders behind the floating sidebar and closes when the sidebar collapses.** The portaled menu is below the floating `
` (which has `z-50`), and moving into the menu leaves the hover wrapper → the sidebar collapses → the expanded `WindowsMenu` unmounts → the menu closes. ### Root Cause `DesktopSidebar`'s hover-float toggles the `sidebarCollapsed` computed, which is used in **`v-if`** to mount/unmount large subtrees: - `AppsSection.vue` renders `ProjectDetailt` under `v-if="!isCollapsed"` (its `isModalOpen` state lives inside, so unmounting kills the modal). - The footer swaps two `WindowsMenu` instances via `v-if="!sidebarCollapsed"` / `v-else`. Portal-based UI launched from these subtrees (the `Modal`, reka-ui menus teleported to ``) lives outside the pointer-hover region, so `mouseleave` fires and collapses the sidebar, destroying the launcher and its state. Confirmed reka-ui behavior: `PopperContent` copies the **computed `z-index` of the content element** onto its fixed wrapper (`zIndex: contentZIndex` in `PopperContent.vue`). So giving `MenubarContent` a higher `z-index` raises the whole portal above the sidebar's `z-50`. ### Strategic Approach - Add a lightweight "interaction lock" in `DesktopSidebar` (`overlayInteractions` counter). While an overlay launched from the sidebar is open, the sidebar stays expanded (so launchers are **not** unmounted). - Bubble `open`/`close` signals from `ProjectDetailt` (via `AppsSection`) and from `WindowsMenu` up to `DesktopSidebar`. - Raise the portaled `WindowsMenu` content `z-index` above the floating sidebar. ### Dependencies & Risks - `ProjectDetailt` is reused in many places (TopBar, KnowledgeView, etc.). Adding `open`/`close` emits is additive and harmless; only `AppsSection` listens. - The counter is guarded with `Math.max(0, …)` to avoid negative drift; open/close are balanced by the reka-ui `openMenu` watcher and the modal's single close path. - `RecentsSection` and other sidebar internals are untouched (out of scope). ### Target Files - `src/components/ProjectDetailt.vue` — emit `open`/`close`, single close path. - `src/components/layout/AppsSection.vue` — bubble `open`/`close` as `overlay-open`/`overlay-close`. - `src/components/layout/DesktopSidebar.vue` — interaction lock + wire events. - `src/components/main-menu/WindowsMenu.vue` — emit `open`/`close`, raise `z-index`. ## 2. Minimum Changes Approach 1. **`ProjectDetailt.vue`**: add `openModal()`/`closeModal()`, emit `open`/`close`; route all close paths (`onProjectSelected`, `onModalClose`) through `closeModal()`. 2. **`AppsSection.vue`**: declare `overlay-open`/`overlay-close` emits and forward `ProjectDetailt`'s `open`/`close`. 3. **`DesktopSidebar.vue`**: add `overlayInteractions` counter + `isInteracting`; make `sidebarCollapsed`/`isFloating` account for it; wire `AppsSection` and both desktop `WindowsMenu` instances to `onOverlayOpen`/`onOverlayClose`. 4. **`WindowsMenu.vue`**: watch `openMenu` to emit `open`/`close`; add `relative z-[150]` to `MenubarContent`. ## 3. File changes, Code Block Formatting & Proposed Changes ```vue src/components/ProjectDetailt.vue ``` | File Path | Action | Component / Section | Change Description | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `src/components/ProjectDetailt.vue` | Modify | `emits` | Added `open` and `close` events so the sidebar can lock its expansion while the modal is open. | | `src/components/ProjectDetailt.vue` | Modify | template trigger button | `@click="isModalOpen = true"` → `@click="openModal"`. | | `src/components/ProjectDetailt.vue` | Modify | `methods` | Added `openModal()` / `closeModal()`; `onProjectSelected()` and `onModalClose()` now route through `closeModal()` (single close path emits `close`). | ```vue src/components/layout/AppsSection.vue ``` | File Path | Action | Component / Section | Change Description | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `src/components/layout/AppsSection.vue` | Modify | `emits` | Added `overlay-open` / `overlay-close` to bubble the project modal open/close state. | | `src/components/layout/AppsSection.vue` | Modify | `ProjectDetailt` usage | Forward `@open`/`@close` to `overlay-open`/`overlay-close`. | ```vue src/components/layout/DesktopSidebar.vue ``` | File Path | Action | Component / Section | Change Description | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `src/components/layout/DesktopSidebar.vue` | Modify | `data` | Added `overlayInteractions` counter. | | `src/components/layout/DesktopSidebar.vue` | Modify | `computed` | Added `isInteracting`; `sidebarCollapsed` and `isFloating` now also account for open overlays so launchers aren't unmounted. | | `src/components/layout/DesktopSidebar.vue` | Modify | `methods` | Added `onOverlayOpen()` / `onOverlayClose()`. | | `src/components/layout/DesktopSidebar.vue` | Modify | template (desktop) | Wired `AppsSection` `@overlay-open`/`@overlay-close` and both desktop `WindowsMenu` instances `@open`/`@close`. | ```vue src/components/main-menu/WindowsMenu.vue ``` | File Path | Action | Component / Section | Change Description | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `src/components/main-menu/WindowsMenu.vue` | Modify | `emits` | Added `open`; `close` still emitted. | | `src/components/main-menu/WindowsMenu.vue` | Modify | `watch.openMenu` | Emits `open`/`close` on any open-state change (click, outside click, Escape, item selection). | | `src/components/main-menu/WindowsMenu.vue` | Modify | `methods.close` | Only resets `openMenu` (close emission now centralized in the watcher, avoiding duplicates). | | `src/components/main-menu/WindowsMenu.vue` | Modify | `MenubarContent` | Added `relative z-[150]` — reka-ui copies the content's computed z-index onto its fixed portal wrapper, raising the menu above the floating sidebar (`z-50`). | ## 4. Why this fixes both issues - **Project detail modal:** `ProjectDetailt` now emits `open` when the modal opens. `AppsSection` bubbles this to `DesktopSidebar`, which increments `overlayInteractions`. The sidebar then stays expanded (`sidebarCollapsed === false`) even after `mouseleave` fires (because the modal overlay is under the pointer). `ProjectDetailt` is not unmounted and the portaled modal (rendered into the app root, after the sidebar, so it paints above `z-50`) shows correctly. - **WindowsMenu:** Opening the menu emits `open` → lock keeps the sidebar expanded, so the expanded `WindowsMenu` isn't swapped out. The `relative z-[150]` class makes the portaled content's z-index propagate to reka's fixed wrapper, so the menu renders **above** the floating sidebar. When the menu closes, `close` decrements the counter and the sidebar collapses normally if the pointer has left. If you'd like, I can also apply the same `z-index`/lock treatment to the `AppIcon` menu (`src/components/apps/AppIcon.vue`) for consistency, but it's outside the reported scope.

history.summary:
Two bugs in the hover desktop sidebar: (1) clicking project detail opened a modal, but hover-expansion re-created components so the modal never showed, and (2) the WindowsMenu rendered behind the floating sidebar and closed when the sidebar collapsed.

Root cause: `DesktopSidebar`'s hover toggle used `v-if` to mount/unmount `AppsSection` (containing `ProjectDetailt`) and `WindowsMenu`, while portaled overlays (reka-ui menus, `Modal`) lived outside the hover region, triggering `mouseleave` and destroying launcher state.

Fix approach: added an `overlayInteractions` counter in `DesktopSidebar` that keeps the sidebar expanded while an overlay launched from it is open, preventing unmount.

Bubbled `open`/`close` events from `ProjectDetailt` → `AppsSection` → `DesktopSidebar`, and from `WindowsMenu`, so the lock tracks modal and menu state.

Raised `WindowsMenu` content to `relative z-[150]` (reka-ui copies content z-index onto its portal wrapper), rendering the menu above the floating sidebar's `z-50`.

**Conversation Summary**

1. User requested that the Windows menu receive focus on open and close on blur.
2. I explored `WindowsMenu.vue`, `WindowsMenuItems.vue`, and related reka-ui Menubar patterns.
3. I proposed modifying `src/components/main-menu/WindowsMenu.vue` with a trigger ref, content ref, `tabindex="-1"`, and `@focusout`/`@pointerdown` handlers.
4. Added `pointerDownInside` state plus `elOf`, `focusMenu`, `onContentPointerDown`, and `onFocusOut` methods to manage focus and blur behavior.
5. Result: menu focuses on open and closes on blur, while still preserving keyboard-open focus and in-panel clicks.
